rationale: The book's identification equates the Name with the three ark contents as the covenant identity of a house by chaining the ark-Name association (2 Sam 6:2), the house-for-Name promise (2 Sam 7:13; 1 Kgs 8:20-21), and the inventory (Heb 9:4) plus independent definitions of manna/tables/rod. This is a coherent but multi-step inference that goes beyond what the texts state. The strongest counter (Name as the person's revealed character/identity/authority/presence) accounts for the identical verses with fewer leaps: the ark and house are simply associated with or dedicated to the LORD's Name as His dwelling and renown, while the three items remain covenant artifacts inside the ark of the covenant. The counter also handles the chapter's further applications (prayer 'in the name,' 'I never knew you,' hallowed Name, third commandment, bride taking a name) more directly as engagement with the person or assumption of identity/belonging. Because the counter explains the material evidence better overall and with smaller unsupported steps, and because at least three supplied details are strained or under-explained under the book's core, the verdict is UNPERSUADED.
book_core_identification: The Name is the covenant identity of a house, consisting of three things appointed and provided by its Head: the Word (the manna), the covenant law (the stone tables), and the fruitful priesthood (Aaron's budded rod).
book_secondary_elaborations: A counterfeit Name substitutes a different word, covenant, or priesthood
A Name is taken in vain when any of the three is rejected, replaced, or removed
A bride takes her Husband's Name by entering His house, coming under His authority, and obeying Him
strongest_counter_interpretation: A 'name' most commonly symbolizes the essential character, identity, authority, presence, reputation, and power of the person who bears it (supremely the Name of God or of Jesus), so that to know, call on, hallow, trust, or act 'in' the name is to engage with the person himself.
counter_core_identification: Name as the revealed character, identity, presence, reputation, and authority of the person who bears it
material_core_denial: The Name is not constituted by the manna, tables of the covenant, and Aaron's rod as the identity of a house; those are the contents of the ark of the covenant, while the Name itself remains the person/character of the LORD with which the ark and house are associated or dedicated.
counter_case: 2 Sam 6:2 calls the ark by the Name of the LORD of hosts who dwells between the cherubim; this is standard association of the ark with God's presence, not an equation of the Name with the ark's contents.

2 Sam 7:13 and 1 Kgs 8:20-21 speak of a house built 'for my name' / 'for the name of the LORD' into which the ark (containing the covenant) is placed; this is temple dedication to God's presence and renown, not a definition of the Name as the three items.
Heb 9:4 simply inventories the golden pot of manna, Aaron's rod, and the tables inside the ark of the covenant; it never identifies those three as 'the Name'.

Ex 20:7 (name in vain) and Isa 4:1 (women wanting a man's name) are explained by the counter as misuse of divine reputation/identity or assumption of marital belonging, without requiring the three-pillar structure.

The chapter's own applications to 'whatsoever ye shall ask in my name,' the false wonder-workers of Matt 7, Col 3:17, and the Lord's Prayer are more economically read as relating to the person's authority, will, and knowledge of the petitioner than as requiring the manna-tables-rod definition.
book_explanatory_advantages: Tightly unifies the three independently defined ark contents under a single symbol by means of the house-for-Name texts.
Supplies a concrete, testable content for what it means to bear, counterfeit, or empty the Name.
Produces an internally consistent reading of the bride/house/Head motif and of the structure of the Lord's Prayer once the three-item definition is granted.
counter_explanatory_advantages: Requires no extra equating step: co-location or dedication of ark/house with the Name does not make the Name identical to the contents.
Matches the plain grammatical sense of the key verses and the ordinary biblical pattern of Name = person/character/authority.
Explains the same 'in the name,' 'hallowed be thy name,' and 'take the name in vain' texts with fewer redefinitions and no need to map every usage onto manna, tables, and rod.
Avoids over-specifying a broadly used term into the unique historical contents of one container.
evidence_book_core_cannot_explain: 2 Samuel 6:2 predicates the Name of the ark itself ('whose name is called by the name of the LORD'), which the book must re-read as the Name residing in/being the contents; the counter takes the association at face value without contradiction.
Hebrews 9:4 and the surrounding inventory give zero textual warrant that the three items constitute or are called 'the Name'; the identification is imported by the book.

The chapter's opening problem (unanswered prayer 'in my name' and the lawless wonder-workers who claim the Name) is solved by the book only after mapping Name onto Word-covenant-priesthood; the counter solves it directly as failure to act under the person's actual authority and will.
unresolved_objections: The book's overall symbolic method (cross-text pattern establishment) is applied consistently and yields an elegant internal system even if the Name=three equation overreaches the cited evidence.

Secondary motifs (bride taking the Name by entering the house under authority; Name emptied by lawlessness) have independent support from the marriage and obedience texts and would survive even if the three-item core were rejected.
